key_insight: Feature-selection methods identified markedly different prognostic features in glioblastoma, with only five shared across all three approaches.
clinical_relevance: The findings highlight robustness concerns for MRI-based survival biomarkers in glioblastoma, rather than establishing tools for treatment selection or drug discovery.
method: Analysed 463 MRI-derived radiomic, anatomical and clinical features for association with overall survival.
Compared median-split log-rank tests and univariate Cox regression, both Benjamini–Hochberg corrected.
Compared statistical selections with the top 20 features from an XGBoost regressor interpreted using SHAP.
evidence_signal: Across 705 IDH-wildtype glioblastoma patients from three public cohorts, log-rank and Cox analyses selected 99 and 72 features respectively, sharing 51; overlapping selections agreed in effect direction.
watch_item: Many selected features were diagnostic descriptors not restricted to tumour voxels, making descriptor handling and analytical pipeline choices important interpretation concerns.
paper_title: How Robust Are Prognostic Radiomic Features? Comparing Selection Techniques on Pooled Glioblastoma Cohorts
